summary.text: A previously healthy female infant aged 1 year and 2 months, 9 kg, presented with coryza, nasal obstruction, dry cough and continuous fever of 38.5 to 39.4ºC, treated with antipyretics for 5 days. A rash emerged on the second day of symptoms with a decline in general condition, and she was admitted to the pediatric ward.

At admission she was jaundiced, dehydrated and febrile with generalized edema and a diffuse maculopapular exanthema with petechiae. Examination showed a hyperemic left ear canal with fetid effusion, a galloping heartbeat with a holosystolic murmur, tachycardia, blood pressure 108 × 56mmHg, saturation 95% in room air, a palpable liver and Glasgow score 11. Empiric amoxicillin and clavulanate was started.

At the end of the first day she developed toxemia, tachycardia, tachypnea, hypotension and prolonged capillary refill, with a hypothesis of septic shock. After a 20mL/kg crystalloid expansion she was referred to the ICU, where echocardiography showed reduced myocardial contractility, further expansions, epinephrine, intubation and central venous access were used, and TSS was considered, replacing the antibiotics with ceftriaxone and clindamycin. Ear CT suggested acute otitis media.

She stayed hypotensive and received norepinephrine and hydrocortisone, developed multiple organ dysfunction requiring transfusion and vitamin K, and limb findings suggesting necrotizing fasciitis led to a bedside fasciotomy of the left upper limb and cultures. Antibiotics were changed on the third day, and cultures showed S. pyogenes in left-ear secretions. Ventilation was removed, she moved to the ward from day six and was discharged on day 14 with a satisfactory course.

ambiguities.issue: Section b00015 says cultures of skin, subcutaneous tissue and muscles were collected at fasciotomy, while b00017 reports results of "cultures collected at admission" showing only S. pyogenes in left-ear secretions; the source does not report the skin, tissue or muscle culture results or link the two statements.

evidence.quote: Cultures of the skin, subcutaneous tissue and muscles were collected
The results of the cultures collected at admission indicated only the presence of S. pyogenes in the otological secretions of the left ear.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not infer negative skin, tissue, muscle or blood cultures, and do not assume the fasciotomy cultures are the admission cultures.

ambiguities.issue: Dose units are printed as 1mg/kg/ min for norepinephrine and 100m/m2 body surface for hydrocortisone, which look like print errors.

evidence.quote: norepinephrine 1mg/kg/ min followed by hydrocortisone 100m/m2 body surface were administered

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not correct units (for example to mcg/kg/min or mg/m2); they are kept as printed.

ambiguities.issue: The suspended drugs in "maintaining only 0.2mcg/kg/minute of epinephrine suspended together with vancomycin on the fifth day" are read as epinephrine and vancomycin; "the steroid" that was titrated is not named in that sentence (hydrocortisone is the only steroid named earlier), and whether titrating meant reduction or stopping is not stated.

evidence.quote: when it was possible to titrate the vasoactive drug and the steroid, maintaining only 0.2mcg/kg/minute of epinephrine suspended together with vancomycin on the fifth day of intensive care

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not infer that the steroid was stopped or that it was hydrocortisone, or that the vasoactive drug in the titration sentence was only epinephrine.

ambiguities.issue: The case text does not state the side of the fasciotomy; only the Figure 4 caption places the sutured fasciotomy on the left upper limb, and the Figure 3 caption names no limb. The "contralateral limb" with petechiae and bruising is contralateral to the left upper limb named earlier in the same sentence, but the source does not say which limb (upper or lower) it is, and which limb findings were the necrotizing fasciitis site is not stated in the text.

evidence.quote: The patient progressed with hyperemia and generalized edema of the left upper limb, with a capillary refill time > 5 seconds and a weak radial artery pulse, diffuse petechiae and bruising in the lateral region of the contralateral limb suggesting necrotizing fasciitis, and bedside fasciotomy was performed.
Upper limb left after suture of the fasciotomy due to necrotizing fasciitis.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not rename the contralateral limb as the right upper limb, do not assign a side to the limb photographed in Figure 3 from pixels, and do not assign laterality to the necrotizing fasciitis.

ambiguities.issue: Day counting is mixed: "second day of ICU admission", "third day of hospitalization", "fourth day", "fifth day of intensive care", "sixth day of hospitalization" and "14th day" use different or unstated anchors.

evidence.quote: This ear was suppurative on the fourth day
on the 14^(th) day

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not convert these to a single day numbering or order events across different anchors. Only same-anchor pairs are ordered by day number (hospitalization days 1, 3 and 6; ICU days 2 and 5, "ICU admission" and "intensive care" being read as the same ICU stay); the unanchored fourth and 14th days are ordered only by stated sequence words.

ambiguities.issue: The abstract says the cultures, exanthema and necrotizing fasciitis "led to the diagnosis" without naming it; the syndrome is named only in earlier abstract sentences, in the title and in the discussion as general text. The case narrative states only that the authors "considered the possibility of TSS". The positive culture named is from left-ear secretions, a nonsterile site.

evidence.quote: In addition to cultures indicating the etiological agent, the appearance of exanthema and necrotizing fasciitis led to the diagnosis.
we considered the possibility of TSS

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not record a confirmed streptococcal toxic shock syndrome as a scored fact, and do not apply the CDC case classification in Table 1 to this patient.

ambiguities.issue: "Two new expansions were indicated (totaling 60mL/kg)" does not say whether 60mL/kg is the sum of the two new expansions or the total including the earlier 20mL/kg expansion, nor that the new expansions were given.

evidence.quote: Two new expansions were indicated (totaling 60mL/kg)

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not derive a per-expansion volume and do not record the expansions as administered.
